hero.heading: Containers that arrive matching the specification you signed

differentiators.title: Direct sourcing from 300+ growers
differentiators.body: We buy at the farm gate in the clusters each product comes from, not through a mandi agent. That is what makes traceability to a grower block possible when a buyer asks for it.

differentiators.title: In-house pack house, 12 MT per day
differentiators.body: Grading, washing, treatment and packing run under our own supervision rather than a rented line, so a specification change does not need a third party to agree to it.

differentiators.title: Cold chain from field to port
differentiators.body: Pre-cooling within hours of harvest, reefer transport to the port, and a set point logged at stuffing. The temperature record travels with the documents.

differentiators.title: Full documentation set on every shipment
differentiators.body: Invoice, packing list, B/L, certificate of origin, phytosanitary or fumigation certificate, certificate of analysis and insurance — prepared as one set, not chased after the vessel sails.

differentiators.title: Third-party lab reports before dispatch
differentiators.body: Residue, moisture, aflatoxin and microbiological testing at NABL-accredited labs, with the report issued before the container is sealed rather than after arrival.

differentiators.title: 48-hour quote turnaround
differentiators.body: A complete inquiry — product, quantity, destination port, Incoterm — is quoted within two working days. If we cannot supply it, we say so in the same window.

testimonials.quote: The specification we agreed at sample stage is the specification that arrived. Six containers in, we have not had to open a claim.

infrastructure.name: Pack House
infrastructure.body: Washing, grading, treatment and packing lines with weight-based sizing and a dedicated area for buyer-specific packing formats.

infrastructure.name: Cold Storage
infrastructure.body: Independently controlled chambers running from 0 °C to 14 °C so mango, pomegranate, grapes and banana can be held simultaneously at their own set points.

infrastructure.name: Dry Warehouse
infrastructure.body: Humidity-controlled storage for spices, dehydrated vegetables and powders, with segregated bays to prevent aroma transfer between lots.

infrastructure.name: Fumigation & Loading Bay
infrastructure.body: On-site fumigation chamber and ISPM-15 pallet handling, with a dock-level loading bay so reefers are stuffed without breaking the cold chain.

story: The company started as a single-product trading operation, shipping dried turmeric to one buyer in Dubai against an LC at sight. There was no pack house and no cold store — material was bought, cleaned by a third party, and stuffed at a CFS. It worked because the specification was simple and the buyer checked everything.

The limits showed up the first time a buyer asked for something specific: a curcumin percentage, then a residue report, then a packing format nobody at the cleaning yard wanted to change for one container. Bringing grading and packing in-house was less a growth decision than the only way to keep saying yes.

Cold storage came next, and with it fresh produce — mango and pomegranate first, then grapes and banana. Fresh is unforgiving: a broken cold chain is not a quality dispute, it is a total loss, and it teaches process discipline faster than any certification audit. The systems built for fresh produce are the ones now applied to every vertical.

The furniture vertical was added because buyers asked. Jodhpur and Saharanpur workshops were already exporting, but rarely to a single moisture and packing standard. Bringing them under one specification, with kiln drying and ISPM-15 handling controlled centrally, made the difference between a workshop that ships and a supplier a retailer can programme.
vision: To be the supplier an overseas buyer names first when they need Indian produce, spices or furniture — because the specification we quote is the specification that arrives, container after container.

mission.title: Consistent quality
mission.body: Sell against a number, not a description. Curcumin percentage, Brix, moisture, ASTA colour, moisture content in timber — each is agreed before the order and verified before the container is sealed. Where a lot does not meet it, we say so before shipping rather than after.

mission.title: Transparent trade
mission.body: One price, one specification, one set of documents. No quality downgrade between sample and shipment, no charges introduced after the proforma invoice, and a straight answer when we cannot supply what was asked for.

mission.title: Farmer partnership
mission.body: Buy direct at the farm gate, pay on agreed terms, and return the destination market's quality feedback to the grower so the next season's crop is planted against it. A supply base that earns properly is the only one that stays reliable.

mission.title: On-time delivery
mission.body: Book the vessel before confirming the date, not after. Where a delay is unavoidable, the buyer hears it from us early enough to act on it, with the revised ETA and the reason.

motive: India grows and makes far more export-grade product than reaches an overseas buyer intact. The gap is not agricultural — it is the number of hands between the grower and the importer, each taking a margin and none carrying responsibility for what the buyer actually receives.

This company exists to remove those layers. We buy direct from growers and workshops, control the grading, testing and packing ourselves, and sell direct to the importer. The grower is paid a fair, agreed price rather than a residual. The buyer gets a source they can verify, visit and audit.

That is also why the specifications on this site are published in full rather than kept for the quotation stage. An importer comparing three suppliers should be able to see the HS code, the grade, the packing, the loadability and the payment terms before they write the first email. If our numbers do not suit the requirement, that is worth finding out in ten seconds rather than in ten days.

values.name: Integrity
values.body: The lot that ships is the lot that was sampled. Where it is not, the buyer is told before the container leaves.

values.name: Traceability
values.body: Every consignment traces back to a grower block or a workshop, and the record is available on request.

values.name: Punctuality
values.body: Dates are quoted against booked space, and a slipping date is reported early rather than explained late.

values.name: Sustainability
values.body: Reclaimed timber where the design allows it, low-VOC finishes, and packing specified to protect the goods rather than to fill the container.

values.name: Partnership
values.body: Growers on agreed terms and buyers on repeat programmes both plan better than either does on spot transactions.

values.name: Accountability
values.body: A claim is investigated against our own records first. Where the fault is ours, it is settled without arbitration.

export_process.title: Inquiry received
export_process.body: Send the product, quantity, destination port and preferred Incoterm. If any of those are open, we will suggest what suits the route rather than quoting the cheapest option and letting you discover the difference on arrival.

export_process.title: Quotation and samples
export_process.body: A written quotation against a named specification, with packing, loadability and lead time stated. Samples are couriered on request; sample and courier cost is credited against the first container.

export_process.title: Order confirmation and PI
export_process.body: A proforma invoice covering specification, quantity, price basis, payment terms, port of loading and discharge, and expected shipment window. Production starts on LC receipt or on the agreed TT advance.

export_process.title: Procurement, production and QC
export_process.body: Sourcing or manufacture against the confirmed specification, with in-process checks and third-party lab testing where the product calls for it. Buyer or third-party inspection is welcome at this stage.

export_process.title: Documentation and customs clearance
export_process.body: Invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, phytosanitary or fumigation certificate, certificate of analysis and insurance prepared as one set. Draft documents go to the buyer for approval before they are finalised.

export_process.title: Shipment and tracking
export_process.body: Container stuffed under supervision, reefer set point logged where applicable, and the B/L plus complete document set couriered or released against the agreed terms. Container number and vessel details are shared at sailing.

quality_stages.title: Sourcing
quality_stages.body: Grower blocks and workshops are selected on track record and audited before the first purchase. Material is bought against a named specification, not on availability.

quality_stages.title: Incoming inspection
quality_stages.body: Every lot is checked at receipt for moisture, foreign matter, size and visible defects. Lots outside specification are rejected at the gate rather than reworked into a shipment.

quality_stages.title: Grading and processing
quality_stages.body: Weight or size grading, cleaning, Sortex where applicable, and treatment appropriate to the destination. Timber is kiln dried and held at 8–12% before it reaches the packing line.

quality_stages.title: Laboratory testing
quality_stages.body: Residue, aflatoxin, moisture, microbiological and heavy metal testing at NABL-accredited laboratories, against the destination market's limits rather than a domestic minimum.

quality_stages.title: Pre-shipment inspection
quality_stages.body: A sample drawn from the packed consignment is checked against the approved specification and the buyer's sample. Third-party inspection by SGS, Bureau Veritas or Intertek is welcome and the container is held for it.

quality_stages.title: Loading supervision
quality_stages.body: Container inspected for cleanliness and odour, reefer pre-cooled and set point verified, stuffing supervised and photographed, seal number recorded on the packing list.

faqs.question: What is your minimum order quantity?
faqs.answer: It varies by product. Dehydrated products and spices start at 5 MT, moringa powder at 1 MT, furniture at one 20ft container or 50 pieces depending on the item, and fresh produce at one reefer container. Each product page states its own MOQ. Mixed-model containers are accepted in the furniture range.

faqs.question: Which Incoterms do you work on?
faqs.answer: EXW, FOB, CFR and CIF as standard, and CIP on air freight consignments. FOB is the most common for first orders because it gives the buyer control of the freight. We will explain the cost split at quotation if you are unsure which suits your route.

faqs.question: What are your payment terms?
faqs.answer: Letter of credit at sight, or 30% TT advance with the balance against a copy of the bill of lading. Terms for repeat buyers are reviewed after the first two shipments. We do not ship on open account for a first order.

faqs.question: Can I get samples before placing an order?
faqs.answer: Yes. Samples are couriered for dehydrated products, spices and furniture finishes, and the sample plus courier cost is credited against your first container. Fresh produce samples are only meaningful in season and are usually handled as a trial consignment instead.

faqs.question: How long does a shipment take?
faqs.answer: Production or procurement runs from 7 days for fresh produce in season to 75 days for hand-carved furniture. Sea transit is separate: 4–7 days to the Gulf, 18–24 days to North West Europe, 28–32 days to the US East Coast. Both figures are stated in the quotation.

faqs.question: Do you accept third-party inspection?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we hold the container for it. SGS, Bureau Veritas and Intertek all inspect at our facility regularly. Inspection is at the buyer's cost and is worth it on a first order.

faqs.question: What documents come with the shipment?
faqs.answer: Commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, certificate of origin, and then whatever the product and destination require — phytosanitary certificate, fumigation certificate, certificate of analysis, health certificate, insurance certificate, non-GMO declaration. Draft documents are sent for your approval before they are finalised.

faqs.question: Can you supply private label or custom packaging?
faqs.answer: Yes. Buyer-branded cartons and bags are available from 10 MT on dehydrated products, from 1,000–3,000 cartons on fresh produce depending on the format, and on any volume for furniture. Send your artwork and we will confirm the format and any tooling cost.

faqs.question: Do you ship by air?
faqs.answer: On fresh produce, yes — mango and lime move by air from 500 kg where a buyer needs arrival inside 48 hours. Dehydrated products and furniture ship by sea; air freight on those rarely makes commercial sense and we will say so.

faqs.question: How do I start?
faqs.answer: Send the product, quantity, destination port and Incoterm through the contact form or on WhatsApp. A complete inquiry is quoted within 48 hours. If we cannot supply what you need, you will hear that in the same window rather than a week later.
